keyMap.keyedMeaning: What should they wear for a class photo?

approximateSegments.text: Listen to three students. You will hear each speaker's number.
Speaker one, for our class photo, I'd like us to wear the same color.
We don't need to buy anything. I already have a blue shirt and I can wear that.
Different shirts are fine if we all choose blue.
Speaker two, I'd rather let everyone choose their own color for the photo.
I want to wear my green top. We can look like a group without wearing the same thing.
Speaker 3. For me, the important thing is to feel comfortable. We'll be standing
outside for a while. I'm going to wear my warm coat over my shirt.

keyMap.keyedMeaning: Ways to help visitors understand a clothing display.

approximateSegments.text: Listen to three students. You will hear each speaker's number.
Speaker one, for our clothing display, let's put similar materials together.
Visitors could compare cotton clothes in one place and wool clothes in another.
Speaker two, I would put a short written story beside each item. A visitor could read where it
came from and why someone kept it. Speaker three, I would invite the owners to stand
beside their clothes for a short time. Visitors could ask them directly why they
chose those items.
